title: 1988 AHSME Problem 15
statement: If \(a\) and \(b\) are integers such that \(x^2-x-1\) is a factor of \(ax^3+bx^2+1,\) then \(b\) is

solutions.text:
Modulo \(x^2-x-1,\) we have \(x^2\equiv x+1\) and \(x^3\equiv2x+1.\) Thus the polynomial is congruent to \((2a+b)x+(a+b+1).\) Both coefficients must vanish, so \(2a+b=0\) and \(a+b=-1.\) Hence \(a=1\) and \(b=-2.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: A polynomial of degree below \(2\) divisible by the quadratic must be zero
